data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The reliability gain is real and is caused by the checklist preventing the expert's characteristic failure mode \u2014 overconfidence and confirmation bias on configural patterns \u2014 by forcing a serial, exhaustive, low-bias feature check; the panel adds orthogonal value only where configural (interactive) reasoning is required and the checklist provides a cross-feature integration protocol the expert's intuition would skip.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The outcome is purely additive (non-configural), so there are no configural patterns for the expert to mis-gestalt and the mechanism reduces to the simpler algorithmic-advantage case.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist lacks cross-feature integration rules, so the panel is no better than the expert at configural items.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The expert's intuition is well-calibrated and not prone to overconfidence or confirmation bias on this task.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Expert intuition is optimized for fast pattern recognition, which makes it vulnerable to seeing a familiar configural gestalt and skipping disconfirming features. The checklist enforces serial, exhaustive feature evaluation, which is slower but less biased. For additive (non-configural) outcomes, the checklist alone captures the mechanism and the panel adds little. For configural outcomes (where the outcome depends on interactions, e.g., 'if A and not-B then outcome, regardless of C'), the checklist must include a cross-feature integration rule; a panel of non-experts applying the rule can catch configural patterns that a single expert's intuition would miss because the expert commits to a gestalt. The distinguishing evidence within a single evaluation is the error pattern on configural vs. additive items: if the panel outperforms the expert only on configural items where a cross-feature rule is specified, the mechanism is bias-correction; if the panel outperforms on all items regardless of structure, the mechanism is aggregation. Compliance-tracking is distinguished by whether the panel gets configural items right for the right reason (matching the cross-feature rule) or merely tracks a surface proxy correlated with the configural pattern.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
